contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you started examining how media is built. Today: figuring out WHO a message is for and WHY it exists!

Every piece of media has a purpose (to inform, persuade, or entertain) and an intended audience (who it's specifically trying to reach), and identifying both helps explain the choices a creator made. The EnergyMax ad from yesterday is clearly meant to persuade, aimed at an audience that feels tired or unmotivated. Read this second example: a news headline reading 'Local School Board Approves New Recycling Program.' Identify this headline's purpose and its likely intended audience, and explain how you can tell.
You just identified a media message's purpose and audience! Tomorrow we'll learn specific techniques used to persuade.

objectives: Identify a media message's purpose (inform/persuade/entertain) and intended audience
Explain how specific clues in the headline reveal purpose and audience
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's EnergyMax analysis briefly.
2. Introduce purpose and audience as two separate questions to ask of any media message.
3. Have the child analyze the recycling-program headline.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's persuasive-techniques lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: contrast the neutral, factual tone of the headline directly against yesterday's emotionally-charged ad language to make the purpose distinction concrete
Ready for more: ask the child to identify who is NOT the intended audience for this particular headline, and why
This lesson deliberately reuses last week's Grade 7 author's-purpose concept (inform/persuade/entertain) at a more advanced, media-specific level
teacherGuide.answerKey: This headline's purpose is to inform, and its likely intended audience is local residents/parents in the community — the neutral, factual tone (stating what happened without emotional language) and the specific local detail ('Local School Board') both signal a straightforward informational purpose aimed at people who live in that community.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 9-10 RI.9-10.6: determining an author's point of view and purpose, continuing this week's media-analysis thread.
